Final categorization: OK

Justification: This is a research article focused primarily on land use and land cover (LULC) prediction under scenarios of population decline in Japan. The study explicitly implements spatially explicit land use modeling at the national scale (Japan as a whole, with 367,705 1-km grid cells). It develops predictive land use models for five land use types and generates future projections under two distinct population distribution scenarios (centralization and decentralization) for the period 2015–2050, thus including multiple future scenarios with quantitative comparison.

The study reports quantitative accuracy metrics for the models (Pearson’s r, MAE, MSE, RMSE) and evaluates model accuracy with test datasets. The outputs include mapped LULC projections available online, demonstrating spatially explicit national-scale implementation.

The paper is not a review article and does not meet any exclusion criteria. It is not purely qualitative, not limited to local/regional scale, nor is it a methodological paper without application. The focus is clearly on national-scale LULC prediction with future scenario analysis.

Therefore, it meets all core inclusion criteria for a research paper and is categorized as OK.
